articles.title: SJAA Member Observation Posts & Reports
articles.summary: The article details two San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) member observation events: a highly successful partial solar eclipse viewing at Houge Park on August 21, 2017, which drew about 500 attendees with numerous telescopes and live video feeds; and an observing session at Mendoza Ranch on July 22, 2017. During the Mendoza Ranch event, member Marilyn Perry actively pursued various Astronomical League programs, observing faint fuzzies, Saturn, and the Swan nebula, and discussed her extensive AL achievements. The piece also briefly features a photo from the total solar eclipse in Oregon.

articles.title: Star Party Reports
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) actively engages in community outreach through two distinct star party programs. The long-running 'School Star Party Central' provides numerous private observing sessions for schools across mid-Santa Clara County, relying on dedicated volunteers and boasting high activity levels. Additionally, SJAA successfully launched its first public 'Pinnacles East Star Party' in collaboration with the National Park Service in July 2017, attracting 200 visitors and initiating efforts to certify Pinnacles East as a Dark Sky Site.

articles.title: Cassini Mission and Saturn Observations
articles.summary: NASA's Cassini spacecraft is concluding its nearly 20-year mission on September 15, 2017, with an intentional plunge into Saturn's atmosphere, marking the end of its "Grand Finale" phase. Media events, including news conferences and live commentary, are scheduled at JPL to cover this historic event. The article also features recent Cassini observations, including an image of Saturn-lit Tethys and a view of Saturn's iconic polar hexagon.

articles.title: Iris Nebula (NGC 7023)
articles.summary: This article details an astrophotography session by Bruce Braunstein, capturing the Iris Nebula (NGC 7023) at the Stellarvue Star Party in June 2017. It provides a comprehensive list of the imaging equipment used, including telescope, camera, mount, software, and accessories. Furthermore, it specifies the detailed framing and integration data, totaling 7.9 hours of exposure.

articles.title: Kid Spot
articles.summary: The 'Kid Spot' article features space-themed jokes and a quiz covering solar eclipses and moon phases, with answers provided. It also presents a timeline of '100 Years of Astronomical Discovery' from 1920-1930, highlighting significant events and scientific breakthroughs like the measurement of Betelgeuse, Einstein's Nobel Prize, and the proposal of Hubble's Constant.

articles.title: Board Meeting Excerpts
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) Board meetings from May to August 2017 covered various operational and strategic topics. Discussions included progress on the Hogue Park application with the City of San Jose, updates to the SJAA membership database and website, and the creation of an AskSJAA mailing list. The Board also addressed equipment matters, such as repairs for a 24-inch donated scope and budgeting for a new scope for the school program, while refining event guidelines and amending club bylaws.

articles.title: SJAA Library & Programs
articles.summary: The article details various programs and resources offered by the San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) for its members and the community. These include an astronomy library, telescope repair sessions, solar observing events, and educational programs like 'Quick STARt' and 'Intro to the Night Sky'. Additionally, SJAA provides a loaner equipment program and fosters an Astro Imaging Special Interest Group with related workshops and field clinics to support both beginner and experienced astronomers.
